name: Al-Qadr
meaning: The Power, The Decree, The Destiny, or The High Esteem
revelation_details: Makkan (Most scholars consider it Makkan, revealed early on to establish the immense value of the Quran and the specific night it was sent down).
core_theme: This Surah is entirely dedicated to the most important night in human history: Laylatul Qadr. It celebrates the revelation of the Quran, explains the mind-blowing spiritual mathematics of God's mercy, and describes the descent of the angels that brings absolute peace to the earth for one single night.
name_origin:
The Surah gets its name from the first verse, which introduces Laylatul Qadr (The Night of Decree/Power).

The Historical Story (The Warrior of Bani Israel): To understand why Allah revealed the concept of "a thousand months," we have to look at a beautiful and authentic historical context mentioned by classical scholars of Tafsir (like Ibn Kathir and Al-Suyuti).

One day, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was telling his companions a story about a deeply devout man from the ancient Children of Israel (Bani Israel). This warrior-monk was so dedicated to God that he spent his nights praying and his days fighting in the path of God for exactly one thousand months (which is over 83 years) consecutively, without ever taking a break.

When the companions heard this, they were amazed, but they also felt a deep sense of sadness and inadequacy. The lifespan of the Muslim community (the Ummah of Muhammad) is generally short - mostly between 60 and 70 years. The companions thought, "How can we ever compete with the people of the past? We simply don't live long enough to worship God for 83 straight years!"

They felt their short lives put them at a massive disadvantage. Seeing their sincere desire to do good and their sadness, Allah responded by revealing Surah Al-Qadr. Allah essentially told them: You don't need 83 years. I will give you a single night that is better than the entire lifetime of that warrior.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Grand Descent and a Lifetime of Worship in a Single Night

points.label: The Majestic Descent
points.detail: Indeed, We sent it [the Qur'an] down during the Night of Decree (Laylatul Qadr).

points.label: The Rhetorical Question
points.detail: And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?

points.label: The Unimaginable Multiplier
points.detail: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Surah Al-Qadr is entirely dedicated to the most sacred, monumental night in human history: the night the final revelation connected the heavens to the earth.
• The Majestic Descent: "Indeed, We sent it [the Qur'an] down during the Night of Decree (Laylatul Qadr)."
• (According to the authentic Tafsir of Ibn Abbas, this means Allah sent the Quran down in its entirety from the Preserved Tablet in the highest heaven to the lowest heaven on this night, and from there it was revealed to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم gradually over 23 years).
• The Rhetorical Question: "And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?"
• (Allah asks this question to emphasize that the true majesty, honor, and value of this night are far beyond human comprehension).
• The Unimaginable Multiplier: "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months."
• (A thousand months is roughly equivalent to 83 years and 4 months - an entire human lifespan. Allah does not say it is equal to a thousand months, but "better" [Khayrun], meaning the reward is boundless).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The word Qadr in Arabic carries profound meanings. It means "Decree" (because the destinies, provisions, and lifespans for the upcoming year are written and handed to the angels on this night). It also means "Power, Honor, and Immense Value," reflecting the majesty of the night itself.
Classical scholars highlight a beautiful wisdom behind verse 3. Authentic traditions mention that the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم was shown the lifespans of the previous nations, which were hundreds of years long. He worried that his Ummah (community), who generally live between 60 and 70 years, could never compete with them in good deeds. Out of His infinite mercy, Allah gifted this community Laylatul Qadr. If a believer catches this one night in worship, they receive the spiritual credit of having worshipped Allah continuously, day and night, for over a lifetime. It is the ultimate divine "shortcut" to Paradise.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Heavenly Invasion and Absolute Peace

points.label: The Descent of the Angels
points.detail: The angels and the Spirit [Angel Jibreel] descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.

points.label: The Night of Safety
points.detail: Peace it is (Salamun hiya) until the emergence of dawn.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah then shifts from the timeline of the night to the incredible, unseen physical reality happening on the earth during those hours.
• The Descent of the Angels: "The angels and the Spirit [Angel Jibreel] descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter."
• (The word used is Tanazzal, which implies a continuous, pouring descent. The earth becomes so crowded with angels that they outnumber the pebbles on the ground).
• The Special Mention of Jibreel: "And the Spirit (Ar-Ruh)."
• (Angel Jibreel is the leader of the angels. He is mentioned separately out of profound honor. He comes down this night to visit the believers who are standing in prayer, a beautiful reunion considering he was the one who first brought the Quran to earth).
• The Night of Safety: "Peace it is (Salamun hiya) until the emergence of dawn."
• (The night is pure safety and goodness. Satan cannot do any evil on this night, and the angels constantly send greetings of peace [Salam] upon the believers worshipping in the mosques and in their homes).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
To truly grasp the magnitude of this night, we must look at the authentic Hadith. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, "Whoever stands (in prayer) during Laylatul Qadr out of faith and in the hope of reward, all of his previous sins will be forgiven." (Sahih Al-Bukhari and Muslim). Just standing in sincere prayer wipes a lifetime of mistakes clean.
Tafsir Ibn Kathir notes the breathtaking imagery of verse 4. The earth, usually filled with noise, conflict, and sin, is completely overtaken by a "heavenly invasion" of pure, luminous angels bringing down the decrees of peace, mercy, and provision for the next year.
Because this night is so heavy with divine mercy, Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) asked the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم what she should say if she knew it was Laylatul Qadr. He taught her the most perfect, comprehensive prayer for a night of blank slates: "Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa, fa'fu 'anni" (O Allah, You are Most Forgiving, You love to forgive, so forgive me) [Sunan At-Tirmidhi].
The Surah closes with "until the emergence of dawn." The peace of this night is temporary, ending when the sun rises. It serves as an urgent reminder for the believer: the gates of unimaginable mercy are wide open, but the clock is ticking, and the dawn is fast approaching. Do not sleep through the most important night of your life.

stories_in_surah.title: The Greatest Event in History (Verses 1-2)
stories_in_surah.content:
The Surah opens with a massive declaration: "Indeed, We sent it [the Quran] down during the Night of Decree."

Allah doesn't even mention the word "Quran." He just says "it." In Arabic rhetoric, when something is so universally grand and important, you don't even need to name it; everyone knows what you are talking about.

The Descent of the Quran: Islamic scholars explain that the entire Quran was sent down from the highest heavens (the Preserved Tablet) to the lowest heaven (the sky of this world) on this single night. From there, the Angel Jibril (Gabriel) brought it down to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) piece by piece over 23 years. This night is the anniversary of the moment the ultimate light of guidance entered the world.

To emphasize how incredibly massive this night is, Allah asks a rhetorical question to wake us up: "And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?" Allah is saying: Your human brain cannot even comprehend the magnitude of what happens on this night. Let Me explain it to you.

deep_dives.title: The Spiritual Mathematics (Verse 3)
deep_dives.content:
Allah then drops the ultimate equation of His mercy: "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months."

Let's break down the math of what this actually means. A thousand months is exactly 83 years and 4 months. That is an entire, long human lifetime.

But notice carefully: Allah doesn't say the night is equal to a thousand months. He says it is better than a thousand months. There is no mathematical cap on God's generosity.

If you spend this one night (just a few hours between sunset and dawn) praying, giving charity, or asking for forgiveness, Allah records it in your book of deeds as if you have been doing that exact same good deed, non-stop, every single second for over 83 years. In just ten years of finding Laylatul Qadr, a believer can rack up over 800 years of pure, uninterrupted worship. It is the ultimate spiritual "cheat code" designed by a deeply Merciful God to help a short-lived humanity reach the highest levels of Paradise.

deep_dives.title: The Angelic Traffic Jam (Verse 4)
deep_dives.content:
So what exactly happens on this night that makes it so powerful? Allah lifts the veil on the unseen world.

"The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter."

• The Spirit: This refers to the Angel Jibril (Gabriel), the chief of all angels. He is so honored that Allah mentions him separately from the rest of the angels.
• The Descent: The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) explained in an authentic hadith that on this specific night, the number of angels that come down to Earth is greater than the number of pebbles and stones on the entire planet.

Because the angels are creatures of pure light and obedience, their massive presence on Earth completely overwhelms the atmosphere. They crowd the skies, fill the mosques, and surround anyone who is praying or remembering God. They descend to execute Allah's decrees for the upcoming year - recording who will live, who will die, who will be given wealth, and who will find peace.

deep_dives.title: Pure Peace Until Dawn (Verse 5)
deep_dives.content:
With billions of angels of light surrounding the earth, what does it feel like? The Surah concludes with one beautiful, soothing word:

"Peace it is until the emergence of dawn."

Unlike other nights where there might be a mixture of good and evil, Laylatul Qadr is a night of absolute, unadulterated peace. Because there is such a heavy presence of angels, the devils are completely paralyzed and unable to cause their usual mischief.

It is a night where the heart feels unusually calm, prayers feel deeper, and the mercy of Allah is so close you can almost touch it. This absolute peace lasts from the moment the sun sets until the very first light of dawn breaks the horizon.

The Action Plan (The Prophet's Habit): Because the exact date of this night is hidden within the last ten nights of the month of Ramadan, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) taught us how to catch it. He didn't just sleep; he would stay awake, worship intensely, and wake his family up to do the same.

And he gave us the perfect, simple prayer to repeat endlessly during those nights. His wife Aisha (ra) asked him, "If I know which night is Laylatul Qadr, what should I say?" The Prophet (pbuh) told her to say: "Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun, tuhibbul-'afwa, fa'fu 'anni." (O Allah, You are the Most Forgiving, You love to forgive, so forgive me).

Surah Al-Qadr teaches us that God doesn't want us to fail. He wants to forgive us so badly that He literally engineered a single night where He practically gives away centuries of reward just for asking.
